Hi! I'd be glad to help you out. I am still figuring stuff out right now, but what really helps is to use Chrome and right-click on something you want to change (like the banner) and select "Inspect Element." From here, you can go through (using your mouse to hover on the left side) and find the CSS code (located on the far right) for a particular object you want to change.

Here is the code I use to change the banner to the single cat (which I will be updating soon):

header {

border-bottom: 2px solid #000000;
background-color: #FFFFFF;
position: relative;
background:url([http://i.imgur.com/slmJBpD.png](http://i.imgur.com/slmJBpD.png)) bottom center;
background-repeat:no-repeat;
height: 225px!important;
z-index: 99;

}

So in all, I use the "Inspect Element" to find the CSS code, then I copy the existing code into the Custom Stylesheet in subverse settings and from there I can edit it to my liking.

If you need some help doing something specific we can try to figure it out together!

Yes, the timer is here in place to prevent bots from spamming saving of changes primarily because CSS field can contain a large amount of data which gets sent to the server and saved into database. A good way to edit the CSS would be to do so in Chrome or Firefox where you can have a live preview of what things will look like. When you're happy with the results, you can then proceed to save changes, rather than saving changes every few seconds while experimenting. The timer limit could be lowered, but there needs to be a timer in place to safeguard this feature.
